summary:
AstraVitals is an offline-first health monitoring platform that empowers astronauts on long-duration missions to independently track, evaluate, and manage their own health without relying on real-time Earth support.

It continuously aggregates critical spaceflight indicators—cardiovascular vitals, bone density, immune markers, radiation exposure, and behavioral health—and flags subtle baseline shifts early. Instead of raw medical jargon, AstraVitals provides clear, actionable countermeasures like targeted exercise, hydration, and sleep protocols.

Because deep-space isolation, altered gravity, and radiation silently degrade human health over time, giving crews autonomous, reliable health intelligence is essential to prevent medical emergencies and ensure mission survival.
details:
What It Does & Tech Stack: Built with React, Python (FastAPI), and SQLite, AstraVitals is a 100% offline edge-computing dashboard that tracks astronaut biometrics (vitals, sleep, radiation) and generates immediate health protocols.

Impact & Benefits: It grants deep-space crews complete medical autonomy. By bypassing severe Earth communication delays, it allows astronauts to catch and reverse physical or mental degradation before it becomes a mission-critical emergency.

Creativity: Instead of displaying complex medical charts that require a doctor to interpret, AstraVitals creatively translates raw physiological data into plain-language, personalized countermeasures (e.g., "increase resistance training" or "adjust hydration").

Key Factors Considered: We prioritized a strictly offline architecture (no cloud reliance), a dark-mode UI designed to prevent alarm fatigue, and clear clinical accessibility for non-medical crew members.
